segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
And for this reason al-Mu'tasim left George from Shebat until Ab in Baghdad,
until he sent to Egypt and investigated.
And when it was confirmed that that rebel had lied with slander,
and that George was truly a king,
he sent for him,
and sent out his forces to meet him.
And when he entered,
he seated him before him and received him well,
and gave him abundant gifts,
and sent him back again with honor to his country.
And Mar Dionysius the Patriarch says:
"At that time I was in Baghdad.
And after I visited al-Mu'tasim in the new city which he had built between the two rivers, the Euphrates and the Tigris,
he sent to me by Sulayman, his physician, that I should go and meet the king of the Nubians.
And when I went with bishops and believers,
I saw an intelligent youth, about twenty years old.
And he made known to me through an interpreter his orthodoxy (righteousness of his faith),
and that he abhorred communion with heretics.
And on Sunday I offered the Holy Sacrifice,
and gave communion to him and to his people.
For they had with them holy vessels and vestments for the Mysteries."
At this time Babek, a Khwarazmian man who had rebelled against the Arabs in Persia,
and had killed myriads of them,
when he was defeated,
his commander-in-chief, Nasir, fled with many of his faction to Theophilus,
and they became Christians.
And in the year 1148
(1148 of the Greeks,
837 of our Lord), Theophilus marched out again to Zibatra,
and pitilessly devastated Arabs, Christians, and Jews alike.
And he passed into the region of Melitene,
and took captives and burned.
And he went and encamped against Samosata.
And there gathered from the Rabi'ah Arabs and from the people of Melitene,
and they went against the Romans.
And the Arabs were defeated,
and four thousand of them fell.
And Theophilus turned back again against Melitene, threatening
that if they did not surrender,
he would do to them as he did to Zibatra.
Then the judge and the notables went out to him,
and brought him gifts,
and also brought out the Roman captives who were in Melitene.
And he broke camp and departed.
And Babek the Khwarazmian rebel, when he saw that his faction was weakened,
loaded his silver and fled with four hundred of his men toward the land of the Romans.
And when he reached Armenia,
a certain patrician whose name was Stephen cajoled him and brought him into his house
